name: A plague and a scapegoat
about: Sickness or famine strikes a real town; its people blame one of their own, often a hedge witch, a midwife or a beggar of that town, and its lord burns them, protects them, or loses the town's love, while the sickness decides whether the fire did any good.
title: The Pestilence of {town}

name: {first} of the Fen
Old {first}
{first} the Herbwife
create.memory: I have healed the sick of {town} with herbs for thirty years. They used to thank me.

fade: The sickness lingers in {town} and then is only one sorrow among many.

beats.speaker: lord
text: Sickness comes to {town}: first the tanners' street, then the market. The death-carts go out at night.
In {town} the bread runs out and the coughing starts. The church bell rings for the dead three times before noon.

memory.lord: The sickness came to {town}, and the people look to me.

beats.speaker: scapegoat
beats.text: In the alehouses of {town} they say the sickness came with {scapegoat}. Someone has chalked a mark on {scapegoat.his} door.

memory.scapegoat: They chalked a mark on my door in {town} and say I brought the sickness.

beats.speaker: lord
beats.text: {lord} has {scapegoat} brought before the people of {town} in chains, to answer for the dying.

memory.scapegoat: {lord} put me in chains before the people of {town}.

beats.text: {scapegoat} burns in the square of {town}. The crowd that bayed for it goes home quiet.

memory.lord: I burned {scapegoat} in the square at {town} to quiet the people.

die.how: I was burned in {town} for a sickness I did not bring.

beats.speaker: lord
beats.text: The fire did nothing. The dying goes on in {town}, and now they whisper that {lord} burned the wrong {scapegoat.man}.

memory.lord: I burned {scapegoat} and the dying did not stop. The people of {town} look at me differently.

beats.speaker: lord
beats.text: The sickness lifts from {town} at last. {lord} has the ashes thrown in the river and calls it justice; nobody contradicts {lord.him}.

beats.speaker: lord
beats.text: {lord} stands at {scapegoat}'s door with a drawn sword and says the first man to touch it hangs.

memory.scapegoat: {lord} stood at my door with a sword when all {town} wanted me dead.
memory.lord: I stood between the people of {town} and {scapegoat}.

beats.speaker: lord
beats.text: {lord} finds no proof against {scapegoat} and lets {scapegoat.him} go. The crowd outside does not agree.
The hungry of {town} riot. They break open {lord}'s granary and come for {scapegoat} with torches.

memory.lord: The people of {town} broke my granary and hunted {scapegoat} through the streets.

die.how: The mob of {town} dragged me from my house.

beats.text: {scapegoat} is gone from {town} by morning, over the wall with what {scapegoat.he} could carry. The sickness stays a while longer, and then it too is gone.

beats.speaker: lord
beats.text: {scapegoat} is dead, killed by the people {scapegoat.he} lived among in {town}. {lord} hangs two of them, and it changes nothing.

memory.lord: The people of {town} murdered {scapegoat} and I could not stop them.

beats.text: The sickness burns itself out. Nobody in {town} speaks of {scapegoat} again, and {lord}'s name is blessed in the churches.
The sickness takes {lord} {lord.himself}. In {town} they say it is judgment, and do not say for what.
